song.name: The Weight of Eternity
song.plot: Victory is won, but the reward is a curse. Vorgos reveals the final condition: Eldrin must guard the stone for 400 years. He grapples with the crushing weight of a life paused, waiting for a hero who isn't born yet.
song.analysis: A new song written for the reworked album, and the emotional gut-punch of the finale. Directly continues Heart of War: "The beast is tamed, the Stone is mine." Vorgos delivers the cruel condition — not freedom, but a 400-year vigil behind the iron door. Anchored by the countdown ("A hundred years, and then three more"), the human cost in the bridge ("My friends will die, my world will change"), and the outro naming Kael. Suggested song direction: heavy, burdened — slow, crushing tempo, dark minor key, minimal arrangement, resolute-grief mood.

section.name: Verse 1
section.reworked: The beast is tamed, the Stone is mine, I wait for Vorgos's design. He steps from time, a storm of grey, "Put down the Stone, and walk away."

section.name: Chorus
section.reworked: The weight of eternity, a heavy crown, To guard the light and settle down. A hundred years, and then three more, To wait behind the iron door.

section.name: Verse 2
section.reworked: I thought I fought to save the day, To keep the darkness far away. But now I see the longer game, A hero with another name.

section.name: Bridge
section.reworked: Time will pass like grains of sand, While I protect this silent land. My friends will die, my world will change, While I remain within this range.

section.name: Chorus
section.reworked: The weight of eternity, a heavy crown, To guard the light and settle down. A hundred years, and then three more, To wait behind the iron door.

section.name: Outro
section.reworked: The weight of time, the weight of stone, I face the centuries alone. For Kael's sake, for future's plea, I bear the weight of eternity.
